content: This document provides a summary of information about the product and does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific use. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice and should not replace consultation with your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Before taking hyoscyamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to atropine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Additionally, this medication may contain alcohol, so caution is advised if you have alcohol dependence or liver disease. This drug may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may increase the risk of heatstroke by reducing sweating. Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, including confusion, drowsiness, unusual excitement, constipation, and difficulty urinating. During pregnancy, hyoscyamine should only be used when clearly necessary. This drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels on all your medications (e.g., allergy or cough-and-cold products) as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Managing digestive disorders may involve lifestyle changes such as stress reduction programs, exercise, smoking cessation, and dietary adjustments to enhance the effectiveness of this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in August 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most up-to-date and complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
